summary: Kickoff between Redwood AE/SE and Veridian procurement + security + legal to align on MSA/DPA expectations, SLA thresholds, pricing approval path, and technical checks for hosted vs private deployment.
transcript:
Meeting header:
Date/Time: 2026-03-21 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~48 minutes
Attendees: Lina (Redwood AE), Ethan (Redwood SE), Samantha (Procurement, Veridian), Amir (CISO), Jordan (Legal Counsel), Priya (Cloud Eng), Marcus (DevOps)
Shared: security packet (link: https://redwood.sec/docs/soc2-dpa-summary.pdf), pilot SOW template (link: /sow/pilot-veridian.md)

Topics: MSA/DPA redlines, SLA definitions (p95/p99), data residency & KMS, SSO/SAML, hosted vs dedicated vs private (VPC/on-prem), pricing path and pilot acceptance criteria, benchmark verification.

[00:00] Lina: Hey everybody, thanks for doing this kick off, really appreciate it. Quick round-robin, who we have?
[00:05] Samantha: Hi Samantha Reed from procurement - I'll be shepherding the contract path.
[00:09] Amir: Amir Hassan, CISO. I'll be focused on DPA/KMS and any security gating.
[00:13] Jordan: Jordan Lee, Legal Counsel, contract review.
[00:16] Priya: Priya Nair, cloud eng, will look at connectivity and egress.
[00:19] Marcus: Marcus Bell, DevOps - I'll help with pilot infra and benchmarking.
[00:22] Ethan: Ethan Wu, SE at Redwood - hi, I'll do the technical deep dives and run the perf tests.
[00:26] Lina: Great. Goal for today is to map out the things that will block procurement and legal so we can get the pricing approved and pilot started.

[02:12] Samantha: We're primarily on a 60-day procurement sprint. Two gating items: DPA redlines that our privacy team can't accept, and SLA minimums - we need p99 guarantees or fallback playbooks. Also, costs must be predictable for forecasting.

[03:05] Lina: Understood. Quick callout on Redwood's standard: hosted API is our default with usage pricing; Dedicated reserved pools are available for committed capacity; Private deployments can be done via VPC or on-prem for regulated workloads. For DPA/MSA redlines we usually accept a small set of enterprise adjustments.

[04:10] Jordan: When you say "small set" can you point to specific clauses? We're worried about data residency, audit rights, and subcontractor flow-downs.

[04:45] Lina: Yes, typical points: audit window, breach notification timing (we aim for 72 hours), subcontractor list for the model runner (we'll share that), and KMS handling - whether you want customer-managed KMS or Redwood-managed with HSM attestations.

[05:30] Amir: For Veridian, any PHI or data that ties to patient records will require customer-managed KMS and audit logs forwarded to our SIEM. We may need proof of SOC2 plus pen-test results.

[06:20] Ethan: On the technical side, we can support customer KMS integrations and we have options: bring-your-own KMS (via HSM/KMS e.g., AWS KMS, GCP CMEK) or use Redwood's keystore with HSM-backed keys. For the latter we can provide attestation and key rotation logs. We'll attach the KMS integration matrix in the packet.

[07:05] Priya: For connectivity, how do you handle VPC peering vs private link? We have strict egress rules and prefer PrivateLink style connections vs public egress.

[07:25] Ethan: We support private connectivity via VPC peering or carrier/private link depending on region. For on-prem we can do an air-gapped deployment but that needs separate procurement. There's also latency/cost tradeoffs - private links may reduce egress but add networking setup.

[08:40] Marcus: Important for our side: how do you guarantee model fallbacks? If the primary model is costlier, will Redwood automatically route to cheaper variant and how is that documented in the SLA?

[09:05] Lina: We have routing policies: you can pin a model version or set policy to failover to a compatible variant. For enterprise SLAs we document fallback behavior in the SOW. SLA metrics are typically availability percentiles and p99 latency windows for given per-request profiles. We can add explicit fallback rules.

[10:30] Jordan: Let's talk SLAs. We need clarity: what is your definition of availability, how are maintenance windows scheduled, and do you offer credits?

[10:55] Lina: Availability is measured at the API gateway level per region over monthly windows; planned maintenance is communicated 30 days in advance for major releases, emergency maintenance we can schedule with rollback. Credits are negotiable for enterprise reserved commitments. We'll include the SLA matrix in the SOW.

[12:40] Amir: Also need to know the retention policy for logs and whether Redwood will retain transcript artifacts. For PHI-related requests, minimal logging is preferred and transcripts should not persist in cleartext without encryption and access controls.

[13:15] Ethan: We can set retention windows per customer and redact transcripts on ingestion if required. There's a configuration knob for KV cache persistence too - we can avoid persistent cache for sensitive prefixes. Note: KV cache was transcribed as 'K V cash' in some older docs, but it's KV cache.

[14:20] Samantha: Pricing: procurement wants a deterministic pathway. We'll need unit economics for token pricing, embedding costs, and reserved capacity pricing. Also, egress fees if data leaves region.

[15:05] Lina: I'll send a pricing path: 1) Pilot time-box with usage credits, 2) If pilot meets acceptance criteria we move to reserved capacity commitment with a tiered discount. Egress is charged based on region and you'll see a separate line item. We'll provide a sample forecast spreadsheet.

[16:10] Priya: Acceptance criteria - need to see latency under a synthetic workload mirroring our average (200 token prompts at 1 RPS per session), and accuracy/regression checks on a small test set.

[16:35] Ethan: Ethan: we can run the perf tests and accuracy eval. For latency we can provide p50/p95/p99 across 5k requests. For evals we'll ingest your test prompts and provide diff/regression report. We'll also include KV cache hit rates and how batching affects latency.

[18:00] Jordan: DPA redlines - our legal team is likely to ask for 30-day breach notification, not 72. Any flexibility?

[18:30] Lina: 72 hours is our baseline but we've occasionally accepted stronger SLA terms with contract language that scopes it to reasonable commercial efforts and includes secure disclosure periods. We'll flag that for legal and propose language.

[19:10] Jordan: Also we need subcontractor list: who are the cloud providers and third-party model providers?

[19:30] Lina: Cloud providers: AWS and GCP in primary regions; we sometimes run inference on partner private infra for Dedicated. Model sources: curated open models and Redwood-verified binaries; any third-party model names will be in the annex. We'll provide a vendor/subcontractor roster.

[20:50] Amir: Pen tests and SOC - can you provide recent SOC2 Type II report and summary pen test dates?

[21:10] Lina: Yes, we'll share SOC2 Type II and a high-level pentest summary after NDA -- the SOC2 link is in the packet we shared. For detailed pentest reports we may need a data sharing agreement - we'll work with your security team.

[22:35] Samantha: Timeline: procurement wants to approve pricing within 30 days, legal needs two weeks to triage the DPA redlines. Is that feasible?

[23:00] Lina: For standard DPA redlines and pricing we can often meet that timeline if we get legal redlines quickly. That's why we want Jordan to flag the showstoppers.

[24:10] Marcus: On the pilot side, what's the expected setup time for a small dedicated pool or VPC connectivity?

[24:35] Ethan: For a hosted pilot with network peering: 1-2 weeks to provision private connectivity and service accounts; dedicated reserved pool may require 3-4 weeks depending on GPU capacity and reservations. On-prem requires procurement and install schedule.

[25:50] Priya: We will definitely lean towards either private link or a VPC peering setup — public API won't pass security.

[27:00] Lina: Noted. We'll mark private link as pilot default unless you want a full on-prem.

[28:10] Jordan: Billing - we need invoicing cadence and support for committed spend with monthly true-ups.

[28:35] Lina: We support monthly invoicing and annual commitments. For reserved capacity we offer a monthly invoice with reconciliation based on usage. We can include forecast lines for FinOps.

[30:00] Samantha: Any export controls or data residency issues for EU patients?

[30:20] Ethan: We have region controls; data processed in EU regions will remain in EU unless routed otherwise. We'll include data residency options in the DPA annex.

[31:40] Marcus: Benchmarks - we need to run the workload in our dev environment but hit the Redwood endpoint to measure real latency. Will you allow test tokens and a sandbox environment?

[32:00] Ethan: Yes, sandbox keys and tooling will be provided. We'll coordinate on sample dataset upload for the eval runs. Keep in mind sandbox will mirror hosted performance; dedicated will differ.

[33:25] Amir: For logging, we require forwarding API access logs to our SIEM. Is that supported?

[33:45] Ethan: We support log forwarding via secure syslog/S3 push with encryption in transit. We'll show how to configure.

[35:00] Samantha: On the DPA redline, we'll send a first pass by Tuesday; Jordan will consolidate.

[35:20] Jordan: Yes, we'll deliver redlines and a short memo with top three must-haves.

[36:05] Lina: Great. To summarize next steps: Redwood shares formal SOW draft + pricing by 2026-03-25, SOC2/DPA packet by 2026-03-24, Ethan runs perf and produces initial benchmark by 2026-03-30. Customer provides DPA redlines by 2026-03-24.

[37:00] Samantha: That timeline should work for procurement. If everything lines up we'll push to finance for pricing approval.

[38:15] Marcus: Quick question about model updates - if you upgrade a model, how are performance regressions handled?

[38:40] Ethan: We have a rollout plan: canary deployments and automatic rollback if regen-tests fail; we also allow model pinning to freeze a version for a customer. We'll document regression monitoring in Redwood Console.

[40:05] Amir: One more security ask: can we get an attestation on key handling and a contact for incident response?

[40:20] Lina: Yes, we'll include an incident response contact and KMS handling attestation in the security packet.

[41:30] Jordan: Do you have a standard limitation of liability cap? We often need that aligned with our procurement policy.

[41:50] Lina: Our standard is a negotiated cap tied to fees; we'll surface typical ranges in the SOW and legal can propose specific numbers.

[43:10] Samantha: If we move to a reserved capacity commitment, what's the lead time to scale?

[43:30] Ethan: Autoscaling within a Dedicated pool is immediate for burst capacity, but adding GPUs to a reserved pool takes provisioning lead time - typically 2-6 weeks depending on region capacity.

[45:00] Lina: Ok, last bit — acceptance criteria for pilot: 1) latency thresholds met on your test set, 2) no critical security gaps per Amir's checklist, 3) DPA redlines agreed or a mitigated plan, 4) pricing path approved by procurement. If those are green we can propose a 3-month pilot SOW.

[46:10] Samantha: Sounds good. We'll aim to get redlines in two business days.

[46:50] Lina: Great — thanks everyone. We'll follow up with the packet and the SOW.
[47:05] Ethan: I'll set up the sandbox credentials and ping Marcus for scheduling the benchmark.

[47:20] Jordan: Thanks all.
[47:30] Amir: Thanks.

[47:40] Meeting end.

Notes: transcription includes typical speech noise; some product names spelled differently in conversation. Referenced artifacts: security packet, SOW template, pricing forecast spreadsheet (links in header).

Recap (from transcript):
- Primary blockers: DPA redlines, SLA caps/definitions, KMS/customer-managed keys requirement for PHI, private connectivity requirement.
- Redwood commitments: share SOC2 + DPA guidance (by 3/24), send SOW + pricing (by 3/25), run perf benchmarks (by 3/30), provide sandbox credentials and log-forwarding config.
